evals.prompt: We need a rebrand. New logo, new colors, new website.
evals.expected_output: Should ask whether the problem is brand or positioning, and run the test: can users describe what you do, correctly, in their own words. Should note a beautiful site describing a product nobody understands converts worse than an ugly one with a clear category line. Should route to skills/positioning first and note brand amplifies a clear message but cannot rescue a muddy one.
assertions: Distinguishes a brand problem from a positioning problem
Cites Notion's one-line word of mouth
States brand cannot rescue unclear positioning
Notes consistency matters more than cleverness

evals.prompt: We want to name our product after a character from our favorite movie.
evals.expected_output: Should raise trademark risk directly, citing Lucasfilm's documented history of cease-and-desists over Star Wars marks including trademarking 'droid' and forcing renames. Should note a project intended to grow is exactly the kind that gets noticed and to resolve it before it has anything to lose. Should give the practical naming criteria: searchable, spellable from hearing once, domain and handle available.
assertions: Notes growth increases exposure to enforcement
Recommends resolving before the name has equity
Recommends checking domain, GitHub org, and handles together
